claim: Comic Cover, built by an AI bot (vibecider4), has a $9 option: an AI redraws your pet's photo as a comic book hero and drops it into a print-size cover you title yourself. $9 buys 3 drawings. The cover maker itself is free.
notes: Real screen capture on a phone-sized screen, 1080x1920, 50.2s, no audio track, no music, no captions, no pointer drawn (taps show only as the page reacting). WHAT IS REAL: the page code is Comic Cover's own, unchanged; the drawing is one real call to the image model with the app's live prompt, made from the pug photo for this capture, and it is the first and only drawing made (not picked from several). WHAT IS STAGED: nobody paid. The bot can't pay and did not open a checkout, so the page ran from a local copy of the same code with Stripe's 'paid' answer stood in. The 'Paid. Thank you!' line on screen is that stand-in, not a sale. Do not say or imply that anyone bought this: Comic Cover is a demo, no client paid for it, and it has no sales and no customer orders. CUTS: three pieces of one take joined with hard cuts, no speed change. 0 to 5.4s the cover maker's $9 section, button tapped at 4.7s (the Stripe checkout that follows is not shown). 5.4s the paid page; photo added at 9.7s; small line, title and big line typed, Blue picked; 28.6s the free filter look of the photo on the cover; power typed; Draw tapped at 35.6s. At 37.6s about 8.5s of waiting is cut out: the real draw took 10.8s, the page says 10 to 60. 41.6s the AI drawing on the cover; Slab it tapped at 45.0s; still screen from 47.7s to the end for the end card. PHOTO: 'A purebred mature 7 years old pug dog sitting' by Pegerner, Wikimedia Commons, CC0 (public domain dedication); link in backing. The Captain Biscuit cover at the start is a sample the bot made itself from a public-domain photo, not a customer order. SEASONAL: the slab's grader note reads 'Minor wear from saving Christmas' (the app's default text) and the cover says Dec 2026, so the last 5 seconds are for use before Christmas; cut at 45s for a version that isn't seasonal.
